_comment: SPEC CPU2017 benchmarks for the Spectre-defense study. Drop each
benchmark's sources at benchmarks/spec2017/<name>/src/ and its run inputs
From a SPEC CPU2017 install, for each <name> below:
(use data/train/input for the longer 'train' workload instead)
'run' is the argv the simulated binary gets; 'cflags' are extra compiler
flags beyond the common set in build_spec2017.sh. 'why' records what each
benchmark contributes to the evaluation. VERIFY the run lines against your
SPEC tree's object.pm / control files -- they are the documented test-input

505.mcf_r.why: Pointer-chasing network simplex. Highest L1D miss ratio of the suite -> the worst case for any delay-on-miss defense and a heavy user of SPT's load-delay path.

519.lbm_r.why: Streaming lattice-Boltzmann. Few branches, regular access -> near-zero speculation shadow; shows the floor of each defense's overhead.

531.deepsjeng_r.why: Alpha-beta chess search. Very high branch-misprediction rate -> stresses SPT's deferred-squash (implicit flow) path hardest.

541.leela_r.why: Monte-Carlo tree search. Branchy and pointer-heavy; a second, independent high-mispredict workload.

508.namd_r.why: Dense FP molecular dynamics. Cache-resident and predictable -> the best case, where a good defense should cost almost nothing.

557.xz_r.why: Compression: mixed integer/branch behaviour with a working set between mcf and namd. Fills the middle of the memory-behaviour range.
